sources.title: Anthropic announces deal with Google, Broadcom, says revenue has tripled - Yahoo Finance
passages: Anthropic has signed an agreement with Google and Broadcom for approximately 3.5 gigawatts of computing capacity built on Google's tensor processing units, with the capacity expected to come online starting in 2027, the company said Monday.
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said during an earnings call last month that Broadcom was providing one gigawatt of Google TPU compute for Anthropic this year, according to CNBC .
Broadcom stock gained as much as 3.6% in after-hours trading following the news.
No financial terms were attached to the agreement.

According to Monday's securities filing, Broadcom flagged that Anthropic's ability to draw on the additional compute hinges on its ongoing commercial performance, and noted that discussions with outside operational and financial partners are underway to support the rollout.
Anthropic has warned the label could cost it billions in lost revenue.
Still, the company's annualized revenue has more than tripled in recent months, driven in part by demand for its Claude Code developer tools and broader enterprise adoption.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Anthropic also said Monday that its revenue run rate has now crossed $30 billion on an annualized basis — more than three times the roughly $9 billion figure it recorded at the ende of 2025.

Enterprise traction has also accelerated: The number of clients committing at least $1 million a year has surpassed 1,000, a threshold Anthropic said is twice what it was reporting around the time of its Series G announcement in February.

Anthropic trains and runs its Claude models across multiple hardware platforms — including AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs — and describes Amazon Web Services as its primary cloud and training partner.
Claude is available on AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Azure Foundry.

extraction.body: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals Broadcom has agreed to lend the AI lab up to $42 billion in convertible notes, covering roughly a third of its $125.2 billion five-year TPU lease commitment. The arrangement ties Broadcom's balance sheet directly to Anthropic's compute buildout just as the company heads toward a public listing. Anthropic's IPO filing shows Broadcom isn't just selling the AI lab chips, it's agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to help pay for them. That blurs the line between vendor and creditor right as Wall Street tries to price the company. Buried in the prospectus Anthropic filed toward its public listing is a number that reframes its entire relationship with one of its biggest suppliers. Broadcom has agreed to lend Anthropic as much as $42 billion through convertible notes, according to Reuters, which first reported the filing's details. Anthropic has made a $125.2 billion, five-year commitment for tensor processing unit computing capacity. The loan is meant to help cover it, which means it handles roughly a third of what Anthropic already owes for the compute it's renting. Here's the twist. The chips themselves are Google's. Broadcom doesn't make TPUs outright, it co-designs them with Google, then layers on a role as lessor and now as lender for the capacity Anthropic is leasing. So Broadcom is simultaneously a hardware partner, a landlord for compute, and a bank: three jobs that don't usually sit inside one company's relationship with a single customer. Anthropic's own prospectus flags the problem. The filing warns that a payment or performance default could make a large share of its lease obligations due immediately. At the very same time, it could limit Anthropic's ability to draw on the $42 billion facility to cover them. In plain terms, the backstop is least available exactly when it's needed most. Anthropic also disclosed it had already deposited restricted cash into an account for Broadcom back in April, with room for more deposits to come. The filing says Anthropic doesn't expect any of the notes to actually be sold before the IPO closes. Frankly, this is the same circularity that's defined AI financing all year, just with a new name attached. Nvidia committed up to $100 billion to OpenAI while also selling it the chips that money would buy. In November, Microsoft and Nvidia together put as much as $15 billion into Anthropic. That was part of a deal where Anthropic agreed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute running on Nvidia systems, a round that valued Anthropic around $350 billion, according to CNBC. Broadcom's $42 billion facility follows the identical shape: the supplier finances the customer so the customer can keep buying from the supplier, and the revenue shows up on both companies' books as real growth. Apollo and Blackstone's $35 billion financing for Anthropic shows how AI compute is becoming a private credit asset, not just a venture capital expense. The deal also highlights how Anthropic is building a different capital strategy as OpenAI moves toward a public listing. - how to finance AI infrastructure with private credit - private credit deals for semiconductor and chip investments What makes the Broadcom version sharper is the scale next to Anthropic's actual business. Anthropic brought in close to $4.6 billion in revenue last year and lost more than $8 billion doing it. It's now carrying roughly $518 billion in total infrastructure obligations stretching out over the coming years. A $42 billion credit line sounds enormous until you set it beside that number, where it covers a slice of a slice. Broadcom projects about $115 billion in AI revenue by 2027 and $230 billion by 2028, with Anthropic becoming its largest compute customer that year. It isn't the first time Broadcom has backed this kind of arrangement either. Apollo and Blackstone raised $35 billion in June to finance Google chip leases, with Broadcom backstopping the senior tranches of that debt, according to reporting at the time. The Anthropic facility is the same instinct applied directly to Broadcom's own customer relationship instead of a third party's. Markets shrugged. Broadcom shares closed Tuesday at $351.19, down about 1%, and ticked up less than half a percent in Wednesday premarket trading, nowhere near the reaction you'd expect for a $42 billion commitment. The stock is still sitting 27% below its June high of $481.57, even with Wall Street's average price target near $532. None of this means the arrangement is fraudulent or even unusual for this stage of the AI buildout. It means the people actually carrying the risk on Anthropic's compute bet are not just its venture investors, they're the chipmaker selling it the hardware and now lending it the cash to pay for that hardware too. When a company's biggest vendor becomes its biggest creditor on the eve of a public listing, that's not a financing footnote. That's the balance sheet talking, and prospective shareholders would do well to listen to what it's actually saying. The loan is meant to help cover it, which means it handles roughly a third of what Anthropic already owes for the compute it's renting. Here's the twist. The chips themselves are Google's. Broadcom doesn't make TPUs outright, it co-designs them with Google, then layers on a role as lessor and now as lender for the capacity Anthropic is leasing. So Broadcom is simultaneously a hardware partner, a landlord for compute, and a bank: three jobs that don't usually sit inside one company's relationship with a single customer. Anthropic's own prospectus flags the problem. The filing warns that a payment or performance default could make a large share of its lease obligations due immediately. At the very same time, it could limit Anthropic's ability to draw on the $42 billion facility to cover them. In plain terms, the backstop is least available exactly when it's needed most. Broadcom projects about $115 billion in AI revenue by 2027 and $230 billion by 2028, with Anthropic becoming its largest compute customer that year. It isn't the first time Broadcom has backed this kind of arrangement either. Apollo and Blackstone raised $35 billion in June to finance Google chip leases, with Broadcom backstopping the senior tranches of that debt, according to reporting at the time. The Anthropic facility is the same instinct applied directly to Broadcom's own customer relationship instead of a third party's. Markets shrugged. Broadcom shares closed Tuesday at $351.19, down about 1%, and ticked up less than half a percent in Wednesday premarket trading, nowhere near the reaction you'd expect for a $42 billion commitment. The stock is still sitting 27% below its June high of $481.57, even with Wall Street's average price target near $532. None of this means the arrangement is fraudulent or even unusual for this stage of the AI buildout. It means the people actually carrying the risk on Anthropic's compute bet are not just its venture investors, they're the chipmaker selling it the hardware and now lending it the cash to pay for that hardware too. When a company's biggest vendor becomes its biggest creditor on the eve of a public listing, that's not a financing footnote. That's the balance sheet talking, and prospective shareholders would do well to listen to what it's actually saying. relevantPassages.text: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals Broadcom has agreed to lend the AI lab up to $42 billion in convertible notes, covering roughly a third of its $125.2 billion five-year TPU lease commitment.
Buried in the prospectus Anthropic filed toward its public listing is a number that reframes its entire relationship with one of its biggest suppliers.
That blurs the line between vendor and creditor right as Wall Street tries to price the company.
Frankly, this is the same circularity that's defined AI financing all year, just with a new name attached.
Nvidia committed up to $100 billion to OpenAI while also selling it the chips that money would buy.
In November, Microsoft and Nvidia together put as much as $15 billion into Anthropic.
That was part of a deal where Anthropic agreed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute running on Nvidia systems, a round that valued Anthropic around $350 billion, according to CNBC.

Broadcom's $42 billion facility follows the identical shape: the supplier finances the customer so the customer can keep buying from the supplier, and the revenue shows up on both companies' books as real growth.
Anthropic's own prospectus flags the problem.
The filing warns that a payment or performance default could make a large share of its lease obligations due immediately.
In plain terms, the backstop is least available exactly when it's needed most.
Anthropic also disclosed it had already deposited restricted cash into an account for Broadcom back in April, with room for more deposits to come.
The filing says Anthropic doesn't expect any of the notes to actually be sold before the IPO closes.
What makes the Broadcom version sharper is the scale next to Anthropic's actual business.
Anthropic brought in close to $4.6 billion in revenue last year and lost more than $8 billion doing it.
It's now carrying roughly $518 billion in total infrastructure obligations stretching out over the coming years.
A $42 billion credit line sounds enormous until you set it beside that number, where it covers a slice of a slice.
The stock is still sitting 27% below its June high of $481.57, even with Wall Street's average price target near $532.

extraction.body: Siri's development over the years has been less than stellar, especially compared to competing voice assistants from Google and Amazon, but if the rumors are true, work on the new Siri update is so much of a hassle that Apple is delaying the release of its next-generation Apple Home products.Last year, notorious Apple scooper Mark Gurman told Bloomberg that the Cupertino-based tech giant had been working on a slew of new home products, including long-overdue updates to their HomePod and HomePod Mini, indoor security cameras, and even a tabletop robot with a motorized arm, all to be controlled by the sound of your voice. SEE ALSO: Apple reveals celebration plans for its 50th birthday This aggressive foray into the smart home market was originally slated to launch last year, but was delayed until spring of 2026. sources.body: LONDON — Police on Thursday arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national on suspicion of plotting a terror attack following a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England that British authorities have linked to Tehran.

extraction.body: LONDON — Police on Thursday arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national on suspicion of plotting a terror attack following a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England that British authorities have linked to Tehran. The 27-year-old man was arrested in London on Thursday, and police have searched two properties in the U.K. capital, Counter Terrorism Policing said in a statement. A 26-year-old British national was interviewed by police “under caution,” which means the interview was recorded and can be used in future prosecutions. On Sunday, five men, all British nationals in their 20s and from London, were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terror offenses close to the RAF Fairford air base, which has been used by American bombers to strike Iran. The suspects have since been released on bail. Police say they found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in three vans linked to the five suspects, but no explosives. Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said the investigation “is hugely complex, and our specialist teams are interrogating multiple lines of inquiry. “As we’ve made clear, we’re looking at all possible angles — including possible foreign state involvement,” she said. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the U.K. sees “strong indications” that Iran played a part in the incident. The base 100 miles west of London has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East, including this year’s war with Iran. Top U.S. officials have criticized the decision to grant five suspects bail, with President Donald Trump saying “I wouldn’t have done that” and Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying a lot of people were “disturbed” by the move. Burnham said authorities have the investigation under “the strongest grip and the closest control,” and British officials had been “talking to counterparts in the United States all week to explain what is happening here, how things are being done.” U.K. officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arsons and other attacks in Britain and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

The 27-year-old man was arrested in London on Thursday, and police have searched two properties in the U.K. capital. extraction.body: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called for an overhaul of the United Nations Security Council to guarantee equitable representation across all regions and to abolish the permanent veto power wielded by its five permanent members. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, Sanchez insisted that the international governing architecture must adapt to reflect current realities: "We need to reform the Security Council so that all of the regions in the world have fair representation, and so that we can do away with the right of veto of the permanent members." Sanchez argued that under the principles of the UN Charter, "no country should be a judge in its own case, no matter how powerful they are." He cautioned that fundamental pillars — peace, sustainability, and equal opportunity —are facing systematic assaults from political actors seeking to drag the world back into a "dark past." Highlighting Spain's foreign policy actions, Sanchez cited sanctions against Russia and Madrid's arms embargo on the Israeli government, reaffirming an "unequivocal" condemnation of the "genocide that Netanyahu is still perpetrating in Gaza." Sanchez denounced what he characterised as a "planned and coordinated demolition attempt" directed at weakening multilateral institutions: "They start by questioning the rules, then they break them, knowing well that nobody will dare to hold them accountable. They cut their contributions to multilateral bodies like this one. They obstruct these organisations' ability to act, so then write them off as useless entities that we can do without." Despite these challenges, he urged member states to rebuild trust in the UN. Turning to succession, Sanchez insisted the next secretary-general should be a Latin American woman — noting that all nine postholders to date have been men — describing it as a "historic debt that we must settle." Addressing migration in the North African enclave of Ceuta, where roughly 72,000 people crossed irregularly in late July, Sanchez pledged Spain will respect human rights rather than "turn migrants into the enemy."

extraction.body: The General Assembly met on Thursday to examine the Security Council’s latest veto , cast by China and Russia over a United States-backed sanctions panel of experts on Iran nuclear facilities. Many nations have called for removing or limiting veto power in the Council, but reform of the 15-member organ remains a work in progress. At last year’s annual veto debate, then-General Assembly president Annalena Baerbock called repeated veto use a “ poster child ” for global gridlock. Thursday’s debate was triggered by the assembly’s landmark veto initiative, established in 2022. Khalilur Rahman, president of the assembly’s 81st session, said the veto initiative “cannot substitute for effective Security Council action”. Each invocation of the initiative “ highlights both the value of this mechanism and the circumstances that make it necessary ” and affirms the assembly’s complementary role, ensuring that veto use is accompanied by transparency, explanation and consideration by the wider membership. While the initiative does not override the veto, it guarantees a public and accountable debate on each use and its implications in the General Assembly, where there is no veto power. During the debate, Deputy Permanent Representative Sun Lei of China said that his delegation voted against the draft resolution to “uphold a correct sense of right and wrong”. The current impasse on the sanctions panel arises from the United States’ unilateral withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action on Iran’s nuclear facilities – the Iran nuclear deal of 2015 – its campaign of “maximum pressure” and its “two rounds of strikes against Iran in the midst of negotiations”. Meanwhile, other delegates argued for extending the panel’s mandate. “No UN Member State should prevent the UN Security Council from functioning properly and being fully operational,” said Hedda Samson, Deputy Head of the European Union delegation, noting that the need for a panel of experts is “even great today”. Following Thursday’s debate, the assembly president will send a summary of discussions back to the Security Council. At the outset of the meeting, Mr. Rahman said the assembly and the council “serve humanity best when they operate in balance”, each fulfilling its distinct but complementary responsibilities under the UN Charter . “ Let us, therefore, use this debate not to exacerbate tensions or assign blame, but to clarify positions, identify common ground for constructive solutions and chart a credible path forward to support dialogue and diplomacy and ultimately restore trust in the organization and its ability to deliver,” he said. extraction.body: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called for an overhaul of the United Nations Security Council to guarantee equitable representation across all regions and to abolish the permanent veto power wielded by its five permanent members. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, Sanchez insisted that the international governing architecture must adapt to reflect current realities: "We need to reform the Security Council so that all of the regions in the world have fair representation, and so that we can do away with the right of veto of the permanent members." Sanchez argued that under the principles of the UN Charter, "no country should be a judge in its own case, no matter how powerful they are." He cautioned that fundamental pillars — peace, sustainability, and equal opportunity —are facing systematic assaults from political actors seeking to drag the world back into a "dark past." Highlighting Spain's foreign policy actions, Sanchez cited sanctions against Russia and Madrid's arms embargo on the Israeli government, reaffirming an "unequivocal" condemnation of the "genocide that Netanyahu is still perpetrating in Gaza." Sanchez denounced what he characterised as a "planned and coordinated demolition attempt" directed at weakening multilateral institutions: "They start by questioning the rules, then they break them, knowing well that nobody will dare to hold them accountable. They cut their contributions to multilateral bodies like this one. They obstruct these organisations' ability to act, so then write them off as useless entities that we can do without." Despite these challenges, he urged member states to rebuild trust in the UN. Turning to succession, Sanchez insisted the next secretary-general should be a Latin American woman — noting that all nine postholders to date have been men — describing it as a "historic debt that we must settle." Addressing migration in the North African enclave of Ceuta, where roughly 72,000 people crossed irregularly in late July, Sanchez pledged Spain will respect human rights rather than "turn migrants into the enemy."

extraction.body: The General Assembly met on Thursday to examine the Security Council’s latest veto , cast by China and Russia over a United States-backed sanctions panel of experts on Iran nuclear facilities. Many nations have called for removing or limiting veto power in the Council, but reform of the 15-member organ remains a work in progress. At last year’s annual veto debate, then-General Assembly president Annalena Baerbock called repeated veto use a “ poster child ” for global gridlock. Thursday’s debate was triggered by the assembly’s landmark veto initiative, established in 2022. Khalilur Rahman, president of the assembly’s 81st session, said the veto initiative “cannot substitute for effective Security Council action”. Each invocation of the initiative “ highlights both the value of this mechanism and the circumstances that make it necessary ” and affirms the assembly’s complementary role, ensuring that veto use is accompanied by transparency, explanation and consideration by the wider membership. While the initiative does not override the veto, it guarantees a public and accountable debate on each use and its implications in the General Assembly, where there is no veto power. During the debate, Deputy Permanent Representative Sun Lei of China said that his delegation voted against the draft resolution to “uphold a correct sense of right and wrong”. The current impasse on the sanctions panel arises from the United States’ unilateral withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action on Iran’s nuclear facilities – the Iran nuclear deal of 2015 – its campaign of “maximum pressure” and its “two rounds of strikes against Iran in the midst of negotiations”. Meanwhile, other delegates argued for extending the panel’s mandate. “No UN Member State should prevent the UN Security Council from functioning properly and being fully operational,” said Hedda Samson, Deputy Head of the European Union delegation, noting that the need for a panel of experts is “even great today”. Following Thursday’s debate, the assembly president will send a summary of discussions back to the Security Council. At the outset of the meeting, Mr. Rahman said the assembly and the council “serve humanity best when they operate in balance”, each fulfilling its distinct but complementary responsibilities under the UN Charter . “ Let us, therefore, use this debate not to exacerbate tensions or assign blame, but to clarify positions, identify common ground for constructive solutions and chart a credible path forward to support dialogue and diplomacy and ultimately restore trust in the organization and its ability to deliver,” he said. The Division for Palestinian Rights is consequently not responsible for the views, positions or discrepancies contained in these texts. On 28 April, at the quarterly open debate of Security Council on the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question, the Vice Chair of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People warned about the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. He also condemned the continuing settler violence in the West Bank and the Israeli authorities’ measures aimed at changing the demographic, religious, and cultural character of East Jerusalem, and called for the full implementation of the New York Declaration . The United Nations (UN) Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific stressed that the situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory is “steadily worsening”, and that rampant settler violence, displacement, and accelerating settlement activity are eroding the prospects for a political process and a resolution to the conflict based on a viable two-State solution. On 27 April, the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process commended the Palestinian Central Elections Commission for successfully administering the 25 April local elections and ensuring a credible process despite significant constraints, including the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the severe movement and access restrictions in the West Bank. UN human rights experts condemned Israel’s law approved by the Knesset on 30 March, which by effectively providing for the death penalty solely against Palestinians constitutes “a discriminatory regime of capital punishment” and a violation of Israel’s obligations under international human rights law. Similarly, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, condemned the law and expressed indignation at the “sharp deterioration in the human rights of Palestinians in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since the start of the regional hostilities on 28 February”. Further, UN human rights experts called to end Israeli military attacks affecting civilian shelters in Gaza and expressed serious concern over the forced displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, stressing that “the scale and pattern of these actions” showed “the ongoing broader policy of ethnic cleansing across the occupied Palestinian territory”. In a 30 April statement, UN human rights experts expressed concern that “Israeli sexual violence has become embedded in Palestinians’ daily lives under occupation”. “It is intersecting, structural and systematic, and operates as a tool of control, subjugation and dispossession”, they said. They stated dismay at the “inaction of the international community that permits total impunity”. In an advocacy brief released on 17 April, the UN Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) reported that deaths of women and girls “reached levels unseen before in previous wars on Gaza”. With a peaking during periods of intensified violence, women and girls continue to be killed despite the October 2025 ceasefire agreement to total of more than 38,000 deaths between October 2023 and December 2025. At the same time, UN Women warned of the deepening health risks for women and girls due to displacement and systematic collapse of reproductive health services, and of the long-term social and protection impact of a rise in women-headed households. The UN Population Fund (UNFPA) sounded the alarm on a surge in child marriage and adolescent pregnancy under the pressure of war. UNFPA analysis showed that child marriage is “increasingly driven by survival, not choice”, as a coping mechanism for families facing extreme poverty and displacement. The World Health Organisation (WHO) confirmed that a person contracted to provide services to it in Gaza was killed on 7 April during a security incident and announced suspension of medical evacuations through Rafah crossing until further notice. The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) expressed outrage at the killing of two truck drivers, whom it had contracted to provide clean water to families in Gaza in an incident on 17 April. The UN Country Team in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and partners condemned the killing and called for the protection of civilians, including humanitarian workers and essential service providers, an obligation under international humanitarian law, to be upheld. On 20 April, the World Bank, the European Union and the UN released the “ Gaza Strip Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment ” (RDNA), which estimates recovery and reconstruction needs at around USD 71.4 billion. On 28 April, the UN launched the Horizon Fund , co-chaired by the Palestinian Prime Minister and the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, to support early recovery and resilience-building efforts, economic revitalization, livelihood recovery, and governance strengthening to promote social cohesion and stability, with a primary focus on Gaza. On 13 April, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that the Israeli authorities reopened Zikim crossing into northern Gaza after its closure for more than 40 days. Collection and offloading activities at this crossing are allowed only on alternating days, however. The Annual Compilation of UN Reports on the Question of Palestine (2025) brings together key UN reports, briefings and technical assessments published in 2025. Prepared by UN entities and its affiliated agencies, it reflects the breadth of work across political, legal, humanitarian, human rights, social, and economic dimensions, highlighting developments in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem. All reports are available on the UNISPAL website. The Annual Compilation of UN Resolutions on the Question of Palestine (2025) presents selected resolutions, decisions and voting records adopted in 2025 by the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council and Human Rights Council. Prepared by DPR, the compilation highlights the ongoing work of the UN system in addressing the question of Palestine. All resolutions are available on the UNISPAL website.

In an advocacy brief released on 17 April, the UN Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) reported that deaths of women and girls “reached levels unseen before in previous wars on Gaza”. With a peaking during periods of intensified violence, women and girls continue to be killed despite the October 2025 ceasefire agreement to total of more than 38,000 deaths between October 2023 and December 2025. At the same time, UN Women warned of the deepening health risks for women and girls due to displacement and systematic collapse of reproductive health services, and of the long-term social and protection impact of a rise in women-headed households.

The UN Population Fund (UNFPA) sounded the alarm on a surge in child marriage and adolescent pregnancy under the pressure of war. UNFPA analysis showed that child marriage is “increasingly driven by survival, not choice”, as a coping mechanism for families facing extreme poverty and displacement.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) confirmed that a person contracted to provide services to it in Gaza was killed on 7 April during a security incident and announced suspension of medical evacuations through Rafah crossing until further notice. The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) expressed outrage at the killing of two truck drivers, whom it had contracted to provide clean water to families in Gaza in an incident on 17 April. The UN Country Team in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and partners condemned the killing and called for the protection of civilians, including humanitarian workers and essential service providers, an obligation under international humanitarian law, to be upheld.

On 20 April, the World Bank, the European Union and the UN released the “ Gaza Strip Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment ” (RDNA), which estimates recovery and reconstruction needs at around USD 71.4 billion. On 28 April, the UN launched the Horizon Fund , co-chaired by the Palestinian Prime Minister and the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, to support early recovery and resilience-building efforts, economic revitalization, livelihood recovery, and governance strengthening to promote social cohesion and stability, with a primary focus on Gaza.

On 13 April, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that the Israeli authorities reopened Zikim crossing into northern Gaza after its closure for more than 40 days. Collection and offloading activities at this crossing are allowed only on alternating days, however.

The Annual Compilation of UN Reports on the Question of Palestine (2025) brings together key UN reports, briefings and technical assessments published in 2025. Prepared by UN entities and its affiliated agencies, it reflects the breadth of work across political, legal, humanitarian, human rights, social, and economic dimensions, highlighting developments in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem. All reports are available on the UNISPAL website.

The Annual Compilation of UN Resolutions on the Question of Palestine (2025) presents selected resolutions, decisions and voting records adopted in 2025 by the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council and Human Rights Council. Prepared by DPR, the compilation highlights the ongoing work of the UN system in addressing the question of Palestine. All resolutions are available on the UNISPAL website.

extraction.body: Greece is the president of the Security Council in October. Council members adopted the provisional programme of work for the month earlier today (1 October). Greece has chosen to organise two signature events. The first is a high-level briefing on emerging technologies , with an emphasis on maritime security, under the “Maintenance of international peace and security” agenda item. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is expected to chair the meeting. The second signature event is a briefing on children and armed conflict to mark the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the children and armed conflict mandate by the General Assembly. Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs Giorgos Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting. Briefings are expected from Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict Vanessa Frazier, UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell, African Union (AU) Special Envoy for Children Affected by Armed Conflict Jainaba Jagne, and a civil society representative. The Security Council will hold its annual open debate on women, peace and security (WPS) in October. Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting, which will be titled “Women, peace and security in the next quarter-century: fulfilling the promise through implementation”. UN Secretary-General António Guterres, UN Women Executive Director Sima Sami Bahous, and a woman civil society representative are the anticipated briefers. The Security Council is also scheduled to hold its annual private meeting with the president of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), Judge Yuji Iwasawa. Tomorrow (2 October), Council members are expected to hold an informal interactive dialogue (IID) on the implementation of resolution 2744 of 19 July 2024, which strengthened the mandate of the Focal Point for Delisting and re-established the Informal Working Group (IWG) of the Security Council on General UN Security Council Sanctions Issues. Yvonne Ching Ling Lee, the Focal Point for Delisting, is expected to brief at the meeting, which is being organised by Greece and Pakistan. This month, the Council will hold its annual briefing on cooperation between the UN and regional and sub-regional organisations , focusing on the AU. Briefings are expected from Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the AU and Head of the UN Office to the AU (UNOAU) Parfait Onanga-Anyanga and AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security Bankole Adeoye. AU Peace and Security Council (AUPSC) members will travel to New York for the 20th annual joint consultative meeting between the Security Council and the AUPSC, to be held on 23 October. (The annual meeting rotates between New York and Addis Ababa, the home of the AU headquarters.) The joint consultative meeting will be preceded by the 11th informal joint seminar of members of the Security Council and the AUPSC on 22 October, which will be held in a retreat format at the Greentree Foundation in Manhasset, New York. Several other African issues are on the programme of work this month. Regarding Sudan , the Security Council is expected to vote on a draft resolution extending the 1591 Sudan sanctions regime. It will also receive the regular 120-day briefing on the situation in the country. A UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) official and Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan Pekka Haavisto are expected to brief. The meeting may also feature a briefing on the work of the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee. If the allocation of subsidiary body chairs is not decided by the time of the meeting, Greece may brief in its capacity as Council president. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. The Council expects to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) , which expires on 31 October. Ahead of the mandate renewal, the Council will hold a private meeting with MINURSO troop-contributing countries, at which Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO Alexander Ivanko will participate. Council members will also receive a briefing in consultations from Ivanko and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara Staffan de Mistura. The Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region , Huang Xia, is expected to provide the biannual briefing to the Council on the implementation of the 2013 Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework (PSC-F) for the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Great Lakes region. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. Council members expect to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) ahead of its 31 October expiry. Prior to that, the Council will hold its bimonthly briefing on the situation in Libya, at which Special Representative and Head of UNSMIL Hanna Serwaa Tetteh is expected to brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. There will be a briefing, followed by consultations, on the work of the UN Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) , which will feature a briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General for the Central African Republic (CAR) and Head of MINUSCA Valentine Rugwabiza. The Council will also hold a private meeting with MINUSCA troop-contributing countries, at which Rugwabiza is expected to participate. Several Middle Eastern issues will be addressed in October. The Security Council will hold its quarterly open debate on “The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question” , which Gerapetritis is expected to chair. The anticipated briefer is Acting Special Coordinator and Resident Coordinator at the Office of the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process (UNSCO) Ramiz Alakbarov. Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific Mohamed Khaled Khiari will also brief Council members in closed consultations on the work of the UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) in the Golan. The Council will also hold its monthly briefing on Yemen . Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg and an official from the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) are expected to brief. A civil society representative may also brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. There will be a meeting on political and humanitarian developments in Syria . The anticipated briefers are Deputy Special Envoy for Syria Claudio Cordone, an OCHA official, and a civil society representative. On Lebanon , Council members are expected to be briefed in closed consultations by Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 1559 . (Adopted in 2004, the resolution called for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Lebanon, the disarmament of all militias, and the extension of government control over the whole Lebanese territory.) Members are also likely to continue considering options for possible arrangements after the termination of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) to support the continued implementation of resolution 1701 , which in 2006 called for a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. The Security Council is expected to hold a meeting on the Iraq-Kuwait file. The meeting will feature a briefing on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 2792 of 17 September 2025, which authorised the appointment of a Senior Representative with a mandate to promote, support, and facilitate efforts to repatriate or return missing Kuwaiti and third country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property. Senior Representative Mari Yamashita is the anticipated briefer. Two issues in the Americas will be discussed this month. The Council expects to renew the 2653 Haiti sanctions regime ahead of its 17 October expiry. It also plans to hold a briefing, followed by consultations, on the situation in Haiti. Briefings are expected from Special Representative and Head of the UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) Carlos Ruiz Massieu, Special Representative for the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) Jack Christofides, and a civil society representative. The Council expects to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia before its 31 October expiry. Ahead of that, it will also hold its quarterly meeting on Colombia. Special Representative and Head of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia Miroslav Jenča is the anticipated briefer. Regarding European issues, the Council will hold its semi-annual briefing on the situation in Kosovo . Special Representative and Head of the UN Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) Peter Due is expected to brief. The semi-annual debate on Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) will be held in October. The Council is also expected to vote at the end of the month on the reauthorisation of the EU-led multinational stabilisation force in BiH (EUFOR ALTHEA) prior to its 1 November expiry. As in previous months, the Council may hold one or more meetings on Ukraine in October. Council members will continue following closely the crisis in the Middle East and any spillover effects, such as disruption to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Additionally, they are likely to continue monitoring developments in Ethiopia. In October, Council members are expected to continue conducting “straw polls” to gauge support for candidates for the position of UN Secretary-General . During today’s press briefing on this month’s programme of work, Ambassador Aglaia Balta (Greece) said that “October is the month when we need to make progress and even agree on the new Secretary-General”. She added that the presidency intends to continue consulting with other Council members on the matter, including on the use of colour-coded ballots. The Division for Palestinian Rights is consequently not responsible for the views, positions or discrepancies contained in these texts. On 28 April, at the quarterly open debate of Security Council on the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question, the Vice Chair of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People warned about the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. He also condemned the continuing settler violence in the West Bank and the Israeli authorities’ measures aimed at changing the demographic, religious, and cultural character of East Jerusalem, and called for the full implementation of the New York Declaration . The United Nations (UN) Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific stressed that the situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory is “steadily worsening”, and that rampant settler violence, displacement, and accelerating settlement activity are eroding the prospects for a political process and a resolution to the conflict based on a viable two-State solution. On 27 April, the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process commended the Palestinian Central Elections Commission for successfully administering the 25 April local elections and ensuring a credible process despite significant constraints, including the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the severe movement and access restrictions in the West Bank. UN human rights experts condemned Israel’s law approved by the Knesset on 30 March, which by effectively providing for the death penalty solely against Palestinians constitutes “a discriminatory regime of capital punishment” and a violation of Israel’s obligations under international human rights law. Similarly, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, condemned the law and expressed indignation at the “sharp deterioration in the human rights of Palestinians in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since the start of the regional hostilities on 28 February”. Further, UN human rights experts called to end Israeli military attacks affecting civilian shelters in Gaza and expressed serious concern over the forced displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, stressing that “the scale and pattern of these actions” showed “the ongoing broader policy of ethnic cleansing across the occupied Palestinian territory”. In a 30 April statement, UN human rights experts expressed concern that “Israeli sexual violence has become embedded in Palestinians’ daily lives under occupation”. “It is intersecting, structural and systematic, and operates as a tool of control, subjugation and dispossession”, they said. They stated dismay at the “inaction of the international community that permits total impunity”. In an advocacy brief released on 17 April, the UN Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) reported that deaths of women and girls “reached levels unseen before in previous wars on Gaza”. With a peaking during periods of intensified violence, women and girls continue to be killed despite the October 2025 ceasefire agreement to total of more than 38,000 deaths between October 2023 and December 2025. At the same time, UN Women warned of the deepening health risks for women and girls due to displacement and systematic collapse of reproductive health services, and of the long-term social and protection impact of a rise in women-headed households. The UN Population Fund (UNFPA) sounded the alarm on a surge in child marriage and adolescent pregnancy under the pressure of war. UNFPA analysis showed that child marriage is “increasingly driven by survival, not choice”, as a coping mechanism for families facing extreme poverty and displacement. The World Health Organisation (WHO) confirmed that a person contracted to provide services to it in Gaza was killed on 7 April during a security incident and announced suspension of medical evacuations through Rafah crossing until further notice. The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) expressed outrage at the killing of two truck drivers, whom it had contracted to provide clean water to families in Gaza in an incident on 17 April. The UN Country Team in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and partners condemned the killing and called for the protection of civilians, including humanitarian workers and essential service providers, an obligation under international humanitarian law, to be upheld. On 20 April, the World Bank, the European Union and the UN released the “ Gaza Strip Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment ” (RDNA), which estimates recovery and reconstruction needs at around USD 71.4 billion. On 28 April, the UN launched the Horizon Fund , co-chaired by the Palestinian Prime Minister and the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, to support early recovery and resilience-building efforts, economic revitalization, livelihood recovery, and governance strengthening to promote social cohesion and stability, with a primary focus on Gaza. On 13 April, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that the Israeli authorities reopened Zikim crossing into northern Gaza after its closure for more than 40 days. Collection and offloading activities at this crossing are allowed only on alternating days, however. The Annual Compilation of UN Reports on the Question of Palestine (2025) brings together key UN reports, briefings and technical assessments published in 2025. Prepared by UN entities and its affiliated agencies, it reflects the breadth of work across political, legal, humanitarian, human rights, social, and economic dimensions, highlighting developments in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem. All reports are available on the UNISPAL website. The Annual Compilation of UN Resolutions on the Question of Palestine (2025) presents selected resolutions, decisions and voting records adopted in 2025 by the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council and Human Rights Council. Prepared by DPR, the compilation highlights the ongoing work of the UN system in addressing the question of Palestine. All resolutions are available on the UNISPAL website.

extraction.body: Greece is the president of the Security Council in October. Council members adopted the provisional programme of work for the month earlier today (1 October). Greece has chosen to organise two signature events. The first is a high-level briefing on emerging technologies , with an emphasis on maritime security, under the “Maintenance of international peace and security” agenda item. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is expected to chair the meeting. The second signature event is a briefing on children and armed conflict to mark the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the children and armed conflict mandate by the General Assembly. Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs Giorgos Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting. Briefings are expected from Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict Vanessa Frazier, UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell, African Union (AU) Special Envoy for Children Affected by Armed Conflict Jainaba Jagne, and a civil society representative. The Security Council will hold its annual open debate on women, peace and security (WPS) in October. Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting, which will be titled “Women, peace and security in the next quarter-century: fulfilling the promise through implementation”. UN Secretary-General António Guterres, UN Women Executive Director Sima Sami Bahous, and a woman civil society representative are the anticipated briefers. The Security Council is also scheduled to hold its annual private meeting with the president of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), Judge Yuji Iwasawa. Tomorrow (2 October), Council members are expected to hold an informal interactive dialogue (IID) on the implementation of resolution 2744 of 19 July 2024, which strengthened the mandate of the Focal Point for Delisting and re-established the Informal Working Group (IWG) of the Security Council on General UN Security Council Sanctions Issues. Yvonne Ching Ling Lee, the Focal Point for Delisting, is expected to brief at the meeting, which is being organised by Greece and Pakistan. This month, the Council will hold its annual briefing on cooperation between the UN and regional and sub-regional organisations , focusing on the AU. Briefings are expected from Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the AU and Head of the UN Office to the AU (UNOAU) Parfait Onanga-Anyanga and AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security Bankole Adeoye. AU Peace and Security Council (AUPSC) members will travel to New York for the 20th annual joint consultative meeting between the Security Council and the AUPSC, to be held on 23 October. (The annual meeting rotates between New York and Addis Ababa, the home of the AU headquarters.) The joint consultative meeting will be preceded by the 11th informal joint seminar of members of the Security Council and the AUPSC on 22 October, which will be held in a retreat format at the Greentree Foundation in Manhasset, New York. Several other African issues are on the programme of work this month. Regarding Sudan , the Security Council is expected to vote on a draft resolution extending the 1591 Sudan sanctions regime. It will also receive the regular 120-day briefing on the situation in the country. A UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) official and Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan Pekka Haavisto are expected to brief. The meeting may also feature a briefing on the work of the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee. If the allocation of subsidiary body chairs is not decided by the time of the meeting, Greece may brief in its capacity as Council president. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. The Council expects to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) , which expires on 31 October. Ahead of the mandate renewal, the Council will hold a private meeting with MINURSO troop-contributing countries, at which Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO Alexander Ivanko will participate. Council members will also receive a briefing in consultations from Ivanko and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara Staffan de Mistura. The Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region , Huang Xia, is expected to provide the biannual briefing to the Council on the implementation of the 2013 Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework (PSC-F) for the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Great Lakes region. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. Council members expect to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) ahead of its 31 October expiry. Prior to that, the Council will hold its bimonthly briefing on the situation in Libya, at which Special Representative and Head of UNSMIL Hanna Serwaa Tetteh is expected to brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. There will be a briefing, followed by consultations, on the work of the UN Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) , which will feature a briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General for the Central African Republic (CAR) and Head of MINUSCA Valentine Rugwabiza. The Council will also hold a private meeting with MINUSCA troop-contributing countries, at which Rugwabiza is expected to participate. Several Middle Eastern issues will be addressed in October. The Security Council will hold its quarterly open debate on “The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question” , which Gerapetritis is expected to chair. The anticipated briefer is Acting Special Coordinator and Resident Coordinator at the Office of the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process (UNSCO) Ramiz Alakbarov. Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific Mohamed Khaled Khiari will also brief Council members in closed consultations on the work of the UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) in the Golan. The Council will also hold its monthly briefing on Yemen . Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg and an official from the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) are expected to brief. A civil society representative may also brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing. There will be a meeting on political and humanitarian developments in Syria . The anticipated briefers are Deputy Special Envoy for Syria Claudio Cordone, an OCHA official, and a civil society representative. On Lebanon , Council members are expected to be briefed in closed consultations by Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 1559 . (Adopted in 2004, the resolution called for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Lebanon, the disarmament of all militias, and the extension of government control over the whole Lebanese territory.) Members are also likely to continue considering options for possible arrangements after the termination of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) to support the continued implementation of resolution 1701 , which in 2006 called for a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. The Security Council is expected to hold a meeting on the Iraq-Kuwait file. The meeting will feature a briefing on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 2792 of 17 September 2025, which authorised the appointment of a Senior Representative with a mandate to promote, support, and facilitate efforts to repatriate or return missing Kuwaiti and third country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property. Senior Representative Mari Yamashita is the anticipated briefer. Two issues in the Americas will be discussed this month. The Council expects to renew the 2653 Haiti sanctions regime ahead of its 17 October expiry. It also plans to hold a briefing, followed by consultations, on the situation in Haiti. Briefings are expected from Special Representative and Head of the UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) Carlos Ruiz Massieu, Special Representative for the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) Jack Christofides, and a civil society representative. The Council expects to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia before its 31 October expiry. Ahead of that, it will also hold its quarterly meeting on Colombia. Special Representative and Head of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia Miroslav Jenča is the anticipated briefer. Regarding European issues, the Council will hold its semi-annual briefing on the situation in Kosovo . Special Representative and Head of the UN Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) Peter Due is expected to brief. The semi-annual debate on Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) will be held in October. The Council is also expected to vote at the end of the month on the reauthorisation of the EU-led multinational stabilisation force in BiH (EUFOR ALTHEA) prior to its 1 November expiry. As in previous months, the Council may hold one or more meetings on Ukraine in October. Council members will continue following closely the crisis in the Middle East and any spillover effects, such as disruption to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Additionally, they are likely to continue monitoring developments in Ethiopia. In October, Council members are expected to continue conducting “straw polls” to gauge support for candidates for the position of UN Secretary-General . During today’s press briefing on this month’s programme of work, Ambassador Aglaia Balta (Greece) said that “October is the month when we need to make progress and even agree on the new Secretary-General”. She added that the presidency intends to continue consulting with other Council members on the matter, including on the use of colour-coded ballots. The Security Council will hold its annual open debate on women, peace and security (WPS) in October. Gerapetritis is expected to chair the meeting, which will be titled “Women, peace and security in the next quarter-century: fulfilling the promise through implementation”. UN Secretary-General António Guterres, UN Women Executive Director Sima Sami Bahous, and a woman civil society representative are the anticipated briefers.
The Security Council is also scheduled to hold its annual private meeting with the president of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), Judge Yuji Iwasawa.

Tomorrow (2 October), Council members are expected to hold an informal interactive dialogue (IID) on the implementation of resolution 2744 of 19 July 2024, which strengthened the mandate of the Focal Point for Delisting and re-established the Informal Working Group (IWG) of the Security Council on General UN Security Council Sanctions Issues. Yvonne Ching Ling Lee, the Focal Point for Delisting, is expected to brief at the meeting, which is being organised by Greece and Pakistan.

This month, the Council will hold its annual briefing on cooperation between the UN and regional and sub-regional organisations , focusing on the AU. Briefings are expected from Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the AU and Head of the UN Office to the AU (UNOAU) Parfait Onanga-Anyanga and AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security Bankole Adeoye.

AU Peace and Security Council (AUPSC) members will travel to New York for the 20th annual joint consultative meeting between the Security Council and the AUPSC, to be held on 23 October. (The annual meeting rotates between New York and Addis Ababa, the home of the AU headquarters.) The joint consultative meeting will be preceded by the 11th informal joint seminar of members of the Security Council and the AUPSC on 22 October, which will be held in a retreat format at the Greentree Foundation in Manhasset, New York.
Several other African issues are on the programme of work this month.

Regarding Sudan , the Security Council is expected to vote on a draft resolution extending the 1591 Sudan sanctions regime. It will also receive the regular 120-day briefing on the situation in the country. A UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) official and Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan Pekka Haavisto are expected to brief. The meeting may also feature a briefing on the work of the 1591 Sudan Sanctions Committee. If the allocation of subsidiary body chairs is not decided by the time of the meeting, Greece may brief in its capacity as Council president. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing.

The Council expects to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) , which expires on 31 October. Ahead of the mandate renewal, the Council will hold a private meeting with MINURSO troop-contributing countries, at which Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO Alexander Ivanko will participate. Council members will also receive a briefing in consultations from Ivanko and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara Staffan de Mistura.

The Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region , Huang Xia, is expected to provide the biannual briefing to the Council on the implementation of the 2013 Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework (PSC-F) for the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Great Lakes region. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing.

Council members expect to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) ahead of its 31 October expiry. Prior to that, the Council will hold its bimonthly briefing on the situation in Libya, at which Special Representative and Head of UNSMIL Hanna Serwaa Tetteh is expected to brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing.

There will be a briefing, followed by consultations, on the work of the UN Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) , which will feature a briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General for the Central African Republic (CAR) and Head of MINUSCA Valentine Rugwabiza. The Council will also hold a private meeting with MINUSCA troop-contributing countries, at which Rugwabiza is expected to participate.
Several Middle Eastern issues will be addressed in October.

The Security Council will hold its quarterly open debate on “The situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question” , which Gerapetritis is expected to chair. The anticipated briefer is Acting Special Coordinator and Resident Coordinator at the Office of the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process (UNSCO) Ramiz Alakbarov.

Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific Mohamed Khaled Khiari will also brief Council members in closed consultations on the work of the UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) in the Golan.

The Council will also hold its monthly briefing on Yemen . Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg and an official from the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) are expected to brief. A civil society representative may also brief. Closed consultations are scheduled to follow the open briefing.

There will be a meeting on political and humanitarian developments in Syria . The anticipated briefers are Deputy Special Envoy for Syria Claudio Cordone, an OCHA official, and a civil society representative.

On Lebanon , Council members are expected to be briefed in closed consultations by Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 1559 . (Adopted in 2004, the resolution called for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Lebanon, the disarmament of all militias, and the extension of government control over the whole Lebanese territory.) Members are also likely to continue considering options for possible arrangements after the termination of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) to support the continued implementation of resolution 1701 , which in 2006 called for a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

The Security Council is expected to hold a meeting on the Iraq-Kuwait file. The meeting will feature a briefing on the Secretary-General’s report on the implementation of resolution 2792 of 17 September 2025, which authorised the appointment of a Senior Representative with a mandate to promote, support, and facilitate efforts to repatriate or return missing Kuwaiti and third country nationals and missing Kuwaiti property. Senior Representative Mari Yamashita is the anticipated briefer.

Two issues in the Americas will be discussed this month. The Council expects to renew the 2653 Haiti sanctions regime ahead of its 17 October expiry. It also plans to hold a briefing, followed by consultations, on the situation in Haiti. Briefings are expected from Special Representative and Head of the UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) Carlos Ruiz Massieu, Special Representative for the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) Jack Christofides, and a civil society representative.

The Council expects to vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia before its 31 October expiry. Ahead of that, it will also hold its quarterly meeting on Colombia. Special Representative and Head of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia Miroslav Jenča is the anticipated briefer.

Regarding European issues, the Council will hold its semi-annual briefing on the situation in Kosovo . Special Representative and Head of the UN Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) Peter Due is expected to brief.

The semi-annual debate on Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) will be held in October. The Council is also expected to vote at the end of the month on the reauthorisation of the EU-led multinational stabilisation force in BiH (EUFOR ALTHEA) prior to its 1 November expiry.
As in previous months, the Council may hold one or more meetings on Ukraine in October.

Council members will continue following closely the crisis in the Middle East and any spillover effects, such as disruption to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Additionally, they are likely to continue monitoring developments in Ethiopia.

In October, Council members are expected to continue conducting “straw polls” to gauge support for candidates for the position of UN Secretary-General . During today’s press briefing on this month’s programme of work, Ambassador Aglaia Balta (Greece) said that “October is the month when we need to make progress and even agree on the new Secretary-General”. She added that the presidency intends to continue consulting with other Council members on the matter, including on the use of colour-coded ballots.

It also offers new clarifications of industry practices and auditing requirements. The newly proposed rule, open for a 60-day public comment period, would also allow for self-custody of crypto assets "under certain circumstances" and permit the use of state-chartered trusts as custodians. The latest move to advance a pro-crypto U.S. securities agenda comes the day before the exit of Commissioner Hester Peirce, who has led the agency's Crypto Task Force since its inception. She leaves on Friday and will be a professor in Virginia, leaving the agency with just two . Hensel and UMass President Marty Meehan signed the five-year memorandum of understanding, according to University of Hawaiʻi System News .

The agreement sets up a framework for the two university systems to pursue joint research, student and faculty exchanges, training programs and other initiatives, rather than locking in any specific projects right away.

extraction.body: The University of Hawaiʻi and the University of Massachusetts have agreed to collaborate on research and education focused on strengthening energy systems, critical infrastructure and national security, with presidents from both systems putting pen to paper Thursday at Bachman Hall on the UH Mānoa campus. UH President Wendy F. Hensel and UMass President Marty Meehan signed the five-year memorandum of understanding, according to University of Hawaiʻi System News . The agreement sets up a framework for the two university systems to pursue joint research, student and faculty exchanges, training programs and other initiatives, rather than locking in any specific projects right away. Potential collaboration areas span cyber-physical systems, microgrids, advanced manufacturing, autonomous systems, maritime technologies and sensing, per the same announcement. The agreement also calls for exploring research and workforce development opportunities aligned with U.S. Department of Defense priorities, with an initial focus on energy resilience and critical-infrastructure protection. The partnership recognizes the shared importance of resilient infrastructure in Hawaiʻi and Massachusetts — two states, the university system noted, with extensive coastal and maritime environments. Hensel said Hawaiʻi has a responsibility to use its expertise and unique position in the islands to address challenges both locally and across the nation, adding that Hawaiʻi is an important place to develop and test solutions that can strengthen resilience. Meehan said the agreement creates opportunities for researchers, faculty and students from both institutions to work together on challenges affecting communities across the country, and that the two university systems share a commitment to research and education addressing real-world problems. He also said the partnership can help prepare students for the workforce of the future. That campus system now includes advanced battery storage alongside the largest behind-the-meter solar array in the state. MassCEC also funded a separate microgrid for the Wakefield Municipal Gas and Light Department, which received over $2.8 million to support its Energy Park project serving Wakefield High School and Northeast Metropolitan Regional Vocational High School.

Hawaiʻi has its own microgrid efforts already underway. Hensel Phelps, Sustainability Partners and the Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation broke ground on two microgrid projects on Oʻahu and Kauaʻi featuring solar canopies, battery storage and EV charging stations, according to Solar Builder Magazine . The Oʻahu system is set to serve HDOT Highways' Oʻahu District Main Office Facility near downtown Honolulu.

The new UH-UMass pact's nod toward Department of Defense-aligned research echoes work already happening at UMass Lowell. The U.S. Navy's Office of Naval Research awarded UMass Lowell and Stony Brook University a grant to advance energy-resilience technologies, with UMass Lowell putting the figure at $6.3 million, while Stony Brook University has separately described an earlier Navy grant for similar energy-resiliency research as totaling $7.36 million and running through fall 2022. Researchers on the UMass Lowell-Stony Brook effort are working across 12 projects in four focus areas: power-grid management, structural health monitoring of energy infrastructure, energy storage and materials, and fuels and power systems.

Crucially, UH News notes the new memorandum is a framework rather than a commitment to specific projects — individual research initiatives between UH and UMass would still need to be developed through separate agreements. Whether any of the listed collaboration areas, from microgrids to autonomous systems, actually advance beyond this starting point will depend on those future deals.

extraction.body: Apple Stores around the world have reportedly started receiving confidential boxes marked with instructions not to open them until October 8, just days before Apple is expected to unveil its new smart home lineup. According to MacRumors , the boxes arrived at Apple retail stores earlier this week carrying “Do Not Open Until October 8” stickers. The publication says it received a tip about the shipments and independently verified their existence. The boxes are believed to contain visual merchandising materials rather than the unannounced products themselves, allowing retail employees to prepare updated graphics, labels, and store layouts ahead of Apple’s next hardware announcements. The October 8 instruction is particularly interesting because it falls five days before Apple’s reported October 13 smart home launch. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported this week that Apple plans to begin a major push into the smart home on October 13, led by its long-awaited smart home hub, commonly referred to as HomePad. The company is also reportedly preparing to introduce the first major HomePod mini update since 2020 and its first new Apple TV set-top box since 2022 on the same date. The Apple Post reported yesterday that HomePad is expected to headline the October 13 announcements , giving Apple an entirely new product category built around the home and its next generation of Siri. MacRumors says Apple Stores are preparing to begin installing the new product presentations from October 8. That doesn’t necessarily mean Apple will announce its new hardware on October 8. Retail merchandising can be prepared in advance of an announcement, particularly when stores need to coordinate changes across multiple locations. It does, however, provide another indication that something significant is happening in Apple’s retail operation ahead of the reported October 13 launch. The shipments also arrive while one major question remains unanswered: whether Apple will introduce its new Home products through another streamed presentation or through Apple Newsroom announcements and accompanying product videos. Apple has yet to announce an October 13 event , despite the date now being linked to HomePad, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K. Apple has used confidential retail shipments ahead of major product changes before, keeping new merchandising and other materials sealed until stores are authorized to begin preparing for an announcement or launch. The company hasn’t confirmed what is inside the latest boxes, and there is no indication from the report that Apple Store employees have been given access to the contents ahead of October 8. With October 8 now emerging as the date Apple Stores can reportedly open the confidential shipments, the days immediately following could provide further clues about how Apple intends to introduce its new smart home lineup. For now, October 13 remains the reported date for Apple’s next hardware announcements, with HomePad, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K expected to lead the company’s biggest smart home push to date. If Apple announces the new devices sometime in the week of Monday, October 5, Apple Stores would need to update their displays for launch on October 13.

There is a possibility that the materials relate to the iPhone Duo , but it seems more likely given their confidentiality and timing that they relate to the rumored launch of Apple's smart home hub , alongside a new Apple TV 4K, and the HomePod mini 2.
Squarish 7-inch screen for controlling smart home products, listening to music, making video calls, and more.

According to MacRumors , the boxes arrived at Apple retail stores earlier this week carrying “Do Not Open Until October 8” stickers.
The publication says it received a tip about the shipments and independently verified their existence.

The Apple Post reported yesterday that HomePad is expected to headline the October 13 announcements , giving Apple an entirely new product category built around the home and its next generation of Siri.
It does, however, provide another indication that something significant is happening in Apple’s retail operation ahead of the reported October 13 launch.
The company hasn’t confirmed what is inside the latest boxes, and there is no indication from the report that Apple Store employees have been given access to the contents ahead of October 8.
MacRumors says Apple Stores are preparing to begin installing the new product presentations from October 8.
Apple has yet to announce an October 13 event , despite the date now being linked to HomePad, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K.
Retail merchandising can be prepared in advance of an announcement, particularly when stores need to coordinate changes across multiple locations.
